summary: Weekly POC sync to review benchmark results vs the baseline provider. Redwood shows lower p99 latency for 512/2k seqs on p4d with int8 quantization and improved throughput when KV-cache and batching enabled. topics: Quantization impact and model variants tested (int8 vs fp16)
Dedicated capacity vs Hosted fallbacks and cost tradeoffs
Security/compliance asks: SOC2, KMS, VPC connectivity
transcript:
[00:00] Alex: hey everyone, thanks for joining the weekly POC sync, we got about 45 minutes, lots to cover. uh quick intros?
[00:12] Mark: Mark here, CTO at Astra Health, Sara and Tom with me.
[00:18] Sara: hey all.
[00:20] Priya: Priya from Redwood SE, I ran the latest benchmarks this morning.
[00:25] Alex: great, Priya can you walk through the results high level?
[00:30] Priya: yeah, so we compared Redwood on p4d with int8 quant to your baseline provider's managed endpoint. For 512 token common chat workload, p50 was 24ms vs baseline 35ms, p95 68ms vs 110ms, p99 130ms vs 260ms, so roughly 2x p99 improvement in many cases. Throughput with 4 concurrent streams was about 1.8k tokens/s sustained vs baseline 1.1k tokens/s.
[01:05] Tom: those p99 numbers look promising, were you using KV cache and batching?
[01:10] Priya: yes we enabled KV-cache and continuous batching, small windowing. We also tested prefix caching for repeated prompts which cut token generation by ~12% in some flows. Note: the baseline runs didn't have KV-cache enabled in their default managed config.
[01:25] Sara: how about the long-form 8k token runs? we saw our latency blow up on baseline after ~3k tokens.
[01:33] Priya: good call, we did a 4k and 8k sequence test but only short runs — on 8k we saw p95 jump but p99 still under baseline for most samples; however we need longer sustained multi-stream tests to be confident. We'll run extended 8k multi-stream overnight.
[01:50] Alex: can you also confirm quantization: int8 vs fp16 differences? any quality regressions?
[01:56] Priya: int8 gave a small latency and throughput win, about 8-12% faster, and our evals on the prompt set showed negligible quality diffs; one or two edge cases where tokenization variance changed wording but not meaning. We're tracking these with a small eval harness.
[02:12] Mark: ok, cost — how does this translate to unit cost? baseline vendor is cheaper per-request today on their shared infra but their latency is higher.
[02:21] Alex: right so tradeoff: their per-token compute is a bit lower now but when you factor in user-facing SLOs and retries, we typically see higher effective cost. Redwood's Optimize recommendations (batching+cache) reduced our per-token bill by ~18% in the tests. We'll include the cost model in the pricing sheet.
[02:40] Tom: for Dedicated: if we reserve capacity, can we get sustained throughput guarantees?
[02:46] Priya: yes Dedicated offers reserved GPU pools; we can set autoscale and burst rules. SLA-backed latency targets are part of the Dedicated contract. For the POC we can set up a small dedicated pool to simulate production.
[02:57] Sara: any blockers on VPC or KMS? we need encryption at rest and customer-managed keys.
[03:04] Alex: Redwood Private supports KMS/HSM and VPC peering for private deployments; for hosted we offer envelope encryption and bring-your-own-KMS integrations. We have SOC2 doc set that Priya will send.
[03:18] Mark: great, please send SOC2 + network diagrams. Also we need audit logs and RBAC examples.
[03:25] Priya: will do — I'll drop links to SOC2 cert, audit log examples, and the security checklist in the shared folder.
[03:33] Alex: back to benchmarks — can you explain the test harness differences so Tom can map to your runs?
[03:40] Priya: sure — we used a synthetic proxy that replays your actual prompts (anonymized) and a fixed concurrency profile: 1/2/4/8 streams, batching window 20ms, kv-cache enabled for repeated prefixes. For baseline we used their suggested client settings but they didn't expose kv-cache in their managed svc. We'll upload raw logs and the JMeter-style traces.
[04:05] Tom: the traces will help. our baseline had slightly different tokenization config — might explain some variance.
[04:12] Priya: yep that can shift token counts and throughput. We'll normalize token counts in the sheet.
[04:18] Sara: any reliability problems during runs? did you see OOMs or timeouts?
[04:23] Priya: no OOMs, a handful of transient 503s during the highest concurrency 8-stream 8k tests but retries smoothed it. Those happened during container spin-ups in scale-up tests. On Dedicated we'd avoid that with reserved pools.
[04:37] Alex: customers sometimes ask about fallbacks — can Redwood autoswap to smaller model if latency spikes?
[04:43] Priya: yes we have smart routing and automatic fallback policies to compatible model variants. You can configure fallback latency thresholds.
[04:50] Mark: what's the recommended model/config for our workloads? we're using a 7B open model baseline.
[04:56] Priya: for similar accuracy, we recommended a 7B quantized variant with int8 + dynamic kv-cache and a 512/2k route; for long documents, a 13B fp16 variant might be safer if you need quality above threshold. We'll add concrete model names in the follow-up doc.
[05:12] Tom: timeline — we are aiming for production pilot in ~8 weeks, security sign-off in 3 weeks.
[05:18] Alex: sounds doable. immediate next week tasks are the extended 8k throughput runs and pricing. we'll also prepare a pilot SOW draft.
[05:26] Mark: ok, as long as we get the pricing and SOC2 artifacts.
[05:30] Priya: i'll run the overnight 8k tests and share results + logs, expect by 2026-09-29.
[05:36] Alex: I'll send the pricing and SOW by Monday 9/28, and Tom can share baseline traces.
[05:42] Sara: quick Q — are there any feature flags to disable prefix caching for certain routes? we have regulated prompts we don't want cached.
[05:49] Priya: yes you can opt-out per route; we have route-level cache controls and per-route retention TTLs. We'll include that in the security doc.
[05:58] Mark: last thing, can we get a short runbook for failover behavior for Dedicated vs Hosted?
[06:04] Alex: yes, we'll include an operations runbook appendix in the SOW.
[06:09] Tom: thanks everyone.
[06:11] Alex: ok recap: Priya runs extended 8k multi-stream tests, Alex sends pricing + SOW + benchmark spreadsheet, Tom uploads baseline traces, Priya shares SOC2 and security checklist. We'll reconvene after the test results, same time next week. Thanks.
[06:28] (call ends)
